title: FAR Module 6 — TBS 1

fields.label: Item 5 — Net Change in Total Assets

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Year-End Adjustment Analysis

Apex Company reports preliminary net income of $420,000 before considering the following year-end adjustments.

Year-End Information

  1. Employees earned $24,000 of salaries that have not been recorded or paid.
  2. The company earned $18,000 of service revenue that has not yet been recorded or billed.
  3. Current-year depreciation expense of $30,000 has not been recorded.
  4. Ending inventory was understated by $12,000 because inventory on hand was accidentally omitted from the count.
  5. A lawsuit loss of $20,000 is probable and reasonably estimable, but has not yet been recorded.

Item 1 — Adjusted Net Income

Item 2 — Accounts Receivable Increase

Item 3 — Inventory Increase

Item 4 — Increase in Liabilities

Item 5 — Net Change in Total Assets
explanation:
Item 1 — Adjusted Net Income

Preliminary Net Income: $420,000

− Accrued Salaries: $24,000

+ Accrued Revenue: $18,000

− Depreciation: $30,000

+ Inventory Correction: $12,000

− Lawsuit Loss: $20,000

Adjusted Net Income = $376,000

Item 2 — Accounts Receivable

The company earned $18,000 of service revenue that had not yet been recorded or billed.

Increase in Accounts Receivable = $18,000

Item 3 — Inventory

Ending inventory was understated because $12,000 of inventory was omitted from the physical count.

Increase in Inventory = $12,000

Item 4 — Liabilities

Two adjustments create additional liabilities.

Salaries Payable: +$24,000

Litigation Liability: +$20,000

Total Increase in Liabilities = $44,000

Item 5 — Net Effect on Total Assets

Three adjustments affect total assets.

Accounts Receivable: +$18,000

Depreciation / Accumulated Depreciation: −$30,000

Inventory: +$12,000

Net Change in Total Assets = $0

Integrated Check

Overall, the adjustments decrease net income by $44,000.

Total assets have $0 net change, while total liabilities increase by $44,000.

Because the $44,000 decrease in net income decreases equity by $44,000:

Change in Assets: $0

Change in Liabilities: +$44,000

Change in Equity: −$44,000

$0 = $44,000 − $44,000

The accounting equation remains balanced.
